ayat: ﴿Ilafihim﴾ is an emphatic restatement; it is a verbal noun of ʾalifa with the long vowel (ālafa), ﴿their journey of the winter﴾ to Yemen, ﴿and﴾ the journey of ﴿the summer﴾ to Syria, every year. They used the two journeys for trade, in order to remain in Mecca to serve the House, which was their pride. They were the descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kinana.

Note: the translation above renders the passage, but I should correct a faithful-rendering issue: the Arabic reads "إيلافهمْ" which I have rendered as "Ilafihim." The terms "ʾalifa" and the rest are transliterated as the passage gives them.

Translation of the passage:

﴿Ilafihim﴾ is an emphatic restatement (ta'kid), and it is a verbal noun of ʾalafa with the long vowel (ālafa), ﴿the journey of winter﴾ to Yemen, ﴿and﴾ the journey of ﴿summer﴾ to Syria, every year. They relied on the two journeys for trade, so that they could remain in Mecca to serve the House, which was their pride. They were the descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kinana.
﴿So let them worship﴾ is linked to لِإيلافِ (*li-ʾīlāf*, "for the familiarity/security of"), and the فاء (*fāʾ*) is extra (زائدة, *zāʾidah*, superfluous). ﴿the Lord of this House﴾

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 106, verse 4:

﴿Who fed them against hunger﴾ i.e., because of it (min ajlih), ﴿and made them safe from fear﴾ i.e., because of it. They used to suffer hunger because nothing was grown in Makkah, and they feared the army of the elephant.
